title: RBAC v2: routing & retention for audit events — implementation notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures detailed implementation notes for RBAC v2-driven routing and retention of audit events. It is intended for engineering and security teams implementing policy->pipeline mappings, index tiering, and backfill processes. It complements the RBAC design spec and the audit schema doc (linked above).

Goals (high level):
- Ensure audit events are persisted with retention aligned to data sensitivity derived from RBAC roles and resource tags.
- Provide deterministic routing to storage/index tiers at write time and safe automated reclassification/backfill when RBAC metadata changes.
- Minimize data loss surface in pipeline failures; make backfills idempotent and observable.
- Maintain queryability for compliance timelines and SIEM exports while controlling cost.

Key concepts and mappings:
- Role sensitivity classification (computed at authorization time): HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW. Computed from RBAC v2 policies + resource labels.
- Retention tiers (policy): 
  - HIGH: 7 years (cold object storage + searchable index snapshot every 30 days)
  - MEDIUM: 2 years (hot index for 90 days, then warm/cold index retention for 23 months)
  - LOW: 90 days (hot index only then delete)
- Routing targets: fast-index (Elasticsearch/Opensearch hot), warm-index (s3-backed searchable shards), cold-archive (object store GCS/Azure blob)
- Event metadata must include: event_id, auth_role_hash, role_version, resource_tags, retention_tier, ingestion_time, source_node, schema_version

Mapping algorithm (pseudo):
1) During authorization, RBAC service returns {role_id, role_version, sensitivity_label}.
2) API gateway attaches role_version and sensitivity_label to audit event headers.
3) Ingestion layer runs a deterministic mapper: sensitivity_label -> retention_tier -> route.
4) If role_version changes after ingestion, event remains in original tier until backfill/repair job reconciles (see backfill policy).

Indexing strategy by tier:
- Hot index (default ingest target): optimized for low-latency writes and queries (sequence length short). Retain full index shards for 90 days. Replication factor 2.
- Warm index: rolled indices with searchable segments; lower replication, slower refresh interval. Snapshot every 24 hours to cold store.
- Cold/Archive: compressed, columnar storage; searchable only via rehydrate + read-only index. Kept for HIGH and MEDIUM according to policy.

Write-time guarantees and idempotency:
- Each event ingested with deterministic event_id (uuid5 on hashed canonical payload+timestamp) to enable at-least-once safe deduplication.
- Ingestion step writes to two targets (index write + append-only object log) in a transaction-like pattern (write obj store first, then index; if index fails, retry indexing from object log). The object log is the ground truth for backfills.
- All writes emit a watermark metric per partition: last_successful_sequence, last_attempted_sequence.

Backfill and reclassification policy (when RBAC metadata changes):
- Triggering events: role policy update with retroactive scope OR resource re-labeling OR explicit compliance request.
- Windowing: default retroactive window is 90 days for automatic reclassification. For HIGH-sensitivity retroactive changes, backfill is 7 years (run-as-approval required).
- Backfill pipeline steps:
  1) Extract candidate events from object log (filter by affected resource ids and time window).
  2) Compute new retention_tier per current RBAC mapping.
  3) For events where tier changes: enqueue to reconciliation queue with job metadata (event_id, old_tier, new_tier, retry_count).
  4) Reconciliation worker performs move/copy operations: index-copy or archive-copy + index-delete if required. Writes reconciliation audit record.
  5) Mark job complete and emit metrics: events_reclassified, events_failed, time_to_reclassify_p95.
- Safety: backfill jobs are idempotent; operations are keyed by event_id. Use optimistic locks where the target index supports versioning.

Failure modes and remediation (practical notes):
- Partial index write (index failed after object-log write): remediation is automatic via reindexer scanning object log for events missing from index. Alert: indexing_lag > 10m and missing_count > 1000.
- Object store outage during backfill: backfills pause and enter retry/backoff. Operators should not force-delete objects. Use cold snapshots to rebuild if snapshot pipeline healthy.
- Role-version skew: if ingestion includes an older role_version due to stale cache, reclass via backfill. Add metric role_version_mismatch_rate; alert > 1%.
- Schema upgrade mismatch: ingestion should attach schema_version. If schema_version > pipeline supported, route to quarantine queue for manual inspection. Include link to schema migration PR.
- Bulk delete race (retention enforcement running while backfill in progress): retention enforcement job must read reconciliation-locked flag per event; events with active reconciliation are excluded until completion to prevent accidental loss.

Operational SLOs and alerts (suggestions):
- Ingestion success rate: >= 99.9% per 1h window. Alert if < 99.5%.
- Indexing lag (time between object-log write and index visibility): p99 < 2 minutes for hot tier, p99 < 24 hours for warm tier.
- Backfill throughput: baseline 250k events/hour for MEDIUM reconcilers; adjust by queue depth. Alert if backlog grows > 24h of expected window.
- Reclassification correctness: sampled audit checks (daily) with 99.95% parity between RBAC-derived tier and stored retention_tier.

Monitoring queries (examples):
- Missing index entries: count(object_log where not exists in index) grouped by retention_tier
- Role_version drift: count(events where role_version != latest_role_version_by_role_id)
- Reconciliation failures: count(recons_jobs where status = failed)

Debug/runbook snippets:
- Quick reindex from object_log for a single resource: 
  1) curl -s "https://ingest-api.internal/v1/reindex?resource_id=R123&window=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z/2025-07-01T00:00:00Z" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"
  2) monitor queue: kubectl -n audit get pods -l app=recons-worker
  3) if stuck: describe failing pod logs: kubectl logs POD -c worker | grep event_id
- Force reclassification (admin-approved): create ticket SEC-XXXX then run the job with --force and small batch_size=1000 to validate before full run.

Cost controls and pruning considerations:
- Use compression and columnar serialization for cold storage. Store minimal searchable fields for cold tier (event_id, timestamp, principal_hash) and full payload in object archive.
- Tier downward moves only allowed after manual review (HIGH -> MEDIUM) to prevent accidental data loss for compliance. Upward moves (LOW->HIGH) can be automatic based on RBAC changes.

Privacy and legal notes:
- HIGH-tier events may contain PII; ensure KMS-wrapped encryption and audit of KMS access. Record KMS key_id on event metadata.
- Deletion requests (DSR) must be fulfilled by scanning object_log and index for event_id and performing targeted deletes across tiers with a deletion record.

Open design questions (action items):
- Should role_version be embedded in the index primary key to make version drift observable? (A: consensus leaning yes; follow-up: update ingestion schema.)
- How to surface reclassification progress to CS/legal for active compliance requests? (A: add a dashboard tile and webhook to compliance ticket.)

Appendix: useful tickets and links
- SEC-4891: RBAC v2 rollout checklist (linked)
- PR 332: initial reindexer implementation (git://repo/internal/audit-pipeline#pr-332)
- Confluence: RBAC v2 Design page (linked)

Owner notes (Priya):
- This is a working doc. Implementation teams: ingesters, reindexer, retention-enforcer, and security must align on the field names before final schema bump. I recommend a staged rollout: enable retention_tier tagging in one region, watch metrics for 48h, then enable global backfill with batch_size limits.

If you are operating on an incident related to this pipeline, tag with #sec-rbac-backfill in the incident Slack channel and ping one of the collaborators listed above.
